findings.title: Concurrent builds for the same key can publish divergent indexes
findings.body: The cache lock now protects only the final map assignment, but there is no per-key build coordination or cache recheck before creating an index. Two concurrent searches for an uninitialized namespace/resource can both observe a cache miss, independently build indexes, and then whichever completes last overwrites `b.cache[key]`. The request using the discarded index continues to query an index that will no longer receive watch-event writes, producing permanently stale search results for that request; for file-backed indexes the concurrent `bleve.New` calls can also contend for the same directory. Use a keyed singleflight/lock and recheck the cache after acquiring it before building.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without its mutex
findings.body: `BuildIndex` now writes `b.cache` under `cacheMu`, while `TotalDocs` ranges over the same map without acquiring an `RLock`. Any caller that collects total documents while an index is being built can trigger Go's concurrent map iteration/write panic (and a race-detector failure). Guard the complete iteration with `cacheMu.RLock()`/`RUnlock()`.

findings.title: Startup index counter is updated concurrently without synchronization
findings.body: Each errgroup worker increments `totalBatchesIndexed` concurrently. With `initWorkers > 1`, these unsynchronized read-modify-write operations are a data race and can lose increments, causing incorrect tracing data and race-detector failures. Use an atomic counter or protect the increment with a mutex.
